issues.detail: The Greek 'ζωντος' (living) is a present participle modifying 'θεου' (God). The Vietnamese translation 'hằng sống' (ever-living/eternal) combined with 'còn lại đến đời đời' (remaining until eternity) slightly alters the grammatical structure. Specifically, 'μενοντος εις τον αιωνα' (abiding into the age/eternity) modifies 'θεου' (God), but the Vietnamese phrasing makes it sound like the 'word' is what remains until eternity, rather than God.
